title: Branching stochastic mechanics. I. Clustering and connected correlations within a branching-process representation of the Schrödinger equation
authors: Eric Dumonteil, Benoît Bischoff, Alain Letourneau, Loïc Thulliez, Corentin Doutre
abstract: Can finite-range correlations hide in the statistics of an extended quantum state? The Schrödinger-Nagasawa transform represents the wave function by positive forward and backward diffusion fields whose product is the Born density. We promote them to branching superprocesses, \(Φ_F\) and \(Φ_B\): diffusion samples stochastic paths, whereas Bohm/Fisher-controlled branching generates genealogies of alternative continuations. With rates evaluated on the prescribed Born density, their means reproduce Schrödinger dynamics exactly. The connected sector exhibits supercritical, critical, and subcritical clustering in confinement and has critical dimension \(d_c=2\) in free space. Stationary eigenmodes remain extended; subcritical clusters acquire the reduced de~Broglie scale. We then let the branching rate respond to the fluctuating product \(Φ_FΦ_B\). In the reciprocal basis, the fields equal a smooth reference \(R\) plus centered fluctuations \(ψ_F,ψ_B\), defining the signed kernel \(C_{\rm FB}(x,y)=\mathbb E_ω[ψ_F(x)ψ_B(y)]\). On the anticorrelated branch, \(ρ_{\rm BSM}(x)=-C_{\rm FB}(x,x)\) is the positive paired density. Stationary recovery requires its diagonal to match the Born profile, while off-diagonal decay defines the correlation range. The pair equation splits into collective and relative sectors: spectral cancellation selects the Born collective mode, while suppression of the leading density fluctuation selects the anticorrelated source channel. With relative diffusivity \(D_{\rm eff}\) and positive relaxation rate \(μ_{\rm FB}\), correlations have screening length \(ξ_{\rm FB}=\sqrt{D_{\rm eff}/μ_{\rm FB}}\). Thus an extended Born density and a finite correlation range can coexist in one stochastic kernel, suggesting particle-like organization.
summary: This paper develops Branching Stochastic Mechanics (BSM) to analyze the quantum state via a branching-process representation of the Schrödinger equation. It shows that by analyzing connected correlations beyond the mean density, one can mathematically demonstrate the coexistence of an extended background density and a finite correlation range. This suggests a mechanism for particle-like organization within quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether finite-range correlations can be hidden within the statistics of an extended quantum state whose low-order moments are fixed by the mean.
main_result: The analysis suggests that an extended Born density and a finite correlation range can coexist within a single stochastic kernel, implying particle-like organization.
method: The Schrödinger equation is reformulated using the Schrödinger-Nagasawa transform and promoted to a Branching Stochastic Mechanics (BSM) framework, which retains higher statistical orders (genealogy) beyond mean dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is quantum mechanics governed by the Schrödinger equation. The analysis uses the SN transform to define forward and backward diffusion fields, which are then treated as branching superprocesses.
key_observables: Born Density ($ho$), Connected Kernel ($C_{FB}$), BSM Paired Density ($ho_{BSM}$), and the correlation screening length ($\xi_{FB}$).
important_parameters: Critical dimension $d_c=2$ in free space; the effective relative diffusivity ($D_{eff}$) and relaxation rate ($\mu_{FB}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the stochastic lift (BSM) captures the necessary higher statistical structure, and that the connected moments accurately describe the inherited dependence.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes describe mathematical structures and diagnostics rather than figure content).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the equivalence between the SN transform and Schrödinger dynamics. It then develops the BSM framework, analyzing the connected sector's clustering properties. Finally, it derives the pair equation, showing how the diagonal matching condition and the finite screening length characterize the coexistence of extended density and finite correlations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful statistical framework (BSM) to analyze quantum correlations beyond mean-field approximations, directly addressing how local structure (finite correlation range) can emerge from global, extended quantum states.
